# Ridge

Frontier model benchmark ledger. Cite source URL and as-of date.

- Snapshot: 2026-11-12
- Index: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 (current AA version since 28 Oct 2026; new scale, so not comparable with v4.3.2, which is kept as an archived board. Models AA has not run on v5.0 are blank. Source: https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/intelligence-benchmarking)
- SWE-bench Verified: Vals stopped running new models on 1 Sept 2026, so its leader is out of date and newer models are blank.
- Terminal-Bench 2.1: Vals moved its index to Terminal-Bench 4.0 on 25 Sept 2026 and archived 2.1, so models released since late September are blank. Source: https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/terminal-bench-2-1
- Terminal-Bench 4.0: Vals AI, Mini-SWE-agent harness, 66 tasks, average of three runs. Replaced 2.1 in the Vals Index on 25 Sept 2026; scores do not compare with 2.1. Source: https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/terminal-bench-4
- Board columns: AA Index v5.0, SWE-bench, CursorBench 4.0, Arena Elo, Terminal-Bench 4.0, Terminal-Bench 2.1 (archived), AA Cyber Index, Harvey LAB-AA v1.1, AA Index v4.3.2 (archived, frozen at 27 Oct 2026)
- AA Cyber Index: Artificial Analysis cyber-defense composite (CWE-Bench-AA, DeepsecBench-AA, CyberGym-E2E-AA). Several frontier models decline many tasks on safety grounds, so their low scores mostly reflect refusals. Score notes give each model's refusal read. Ridge scores only publicly available versions: AA's trusted-access rows (such as GPT-6 Sol Daybreak Blue, added 8 Oct 2026) appear in notes, not as scores. Source: https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/artificial-analysis-cyber-index
- Harvey LAB-AA v1.1: Artificial Analysis' run of Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, 120 private legal tasks. v1.1 (8 Oct 2026) gates on a hallucination check against the source documents, so a task counts only if every rubric item passes and there is no material hallucination. Not part of the AA Intelligence Index, which has no legal component. Source: https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/harvey-lab-aa
- JSON table: /api/ledger.json
- CSV table: /api/ledger.csv
- Catalog: /api/v1
- Leaderboard: /api/v1/leaderboard

Cite the source URL and the as-of date.

News (2026-11-10): AA and Google DeepMind Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark, 200 private visual knowledge-work tasks run in Stirrup. Climb WSR: Claude Fable 5.2 (max) 57%, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) 54%, Claude Opus 5.5 (max) 53%. Not a Ridge board. Source: https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/google-deepmind-multimodal-knowledge-agent
News (2026-11-11): LiveBench 2.0 overall: Claude Fable 5.2 (xhigh) 84.9, GPT-6 Astra 84.5, Claude Fable 5.1 84.0, Gemini 4 Carbon 83.5, Claude Opus 5.5 83.4. Not a Ridge board. Source: https://livebench.ai/
News (2026-11-09): AA Endpoint Accuracy Index v1.1. 24 of 103 open-model API endpoints score statistically below AA's reference deployment; causes include output caps, less reasoning, tool-call handling and timeouts. Not comparable with v1.0. Source: https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/endpoint-accuracy-index-v1-1

News (2026-11-10): The Gross committee released OpenAI's Yang-Mills Lean proof and says it proves the existence of pure Yang-Mills theory under the standard problem statements; the mass gap remains open. Source: https://www.kitp.ucsb.edu/statement-by-the-yangmills-working-group
Desk (2026-11-12): Half-week opinion. Claude Fable 5.2 first rated at 4 stars, Gemini 4 Carbon at 3, Claude Opus 5.5 holds at 5. From public X posts, 9 to 12 November.

Token Plan only, no pay-as-you-go. Preview runs to 24:00 25 November (UTC+8), then the model is retired. No benchmarks, parameter count or price; no independent score, not a Ridge row. Source: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/qwen4-max-preview

New model (2026-11-09): Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic, closed weights, API id claude-fable-5-2). Claude Mythos 5.2 is the same model for organizations in the Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs, not a separate row. $8 / $40 per 1M tokens (Fable 5.1 was $10 / $50), cache reads $0.20, 5-minute cache writes $10, 1-hour cache writes $16, batch $4 / $20. Fast mode (speed set to fast, no beta header) $16 / $80, up to 2.5x output speed. 1M context, 128K max output, adaptive thinking always on. Parameter count not disclosed. Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock (id anthropic.claude-fable-5-2), Google Cloud (Anthropic-managed and Google-managed), Microsoft Foundry, and paid Claude plans. AA Intelligence Index v5.0 65 (max, #1). Arena+ 1538 (#1). CursorBench 4.0 60.0 (max). Harvey LAB-AA 7.2 (#6 of 33). Vals Terminal-Bench 4.0 65.15, tied #1 of 63 with Claude Opus 5.5 (Mini-SWE-agent, high effort; 17 of 198 attempts, 8.59%, were fallbacks). AA Cyber and AA-Robotics are blank. Archived AA v4.3.2 has no Fable 5.2 score. Vals Index 71.31% is Vals' figure, not a Ridge column. Anthropic says standard outputs are up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1. Fable 5.1 stays. Sources: https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2 https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/terminal-bench-4 https://artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models https://cursor.com/cursorbench

Haiku matches that only up to 100K tokens, then $0.50 / $2.50. AA lists Spark 1.3 max at $2.39 per Index task against Ember's $0.14, a per-task gap, not a per-token one. Luna's live index score is 28. Source: https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-ember

News (2026-11-08): Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2 scores a model for being right and for being sure only when it should be. New pieces: AA-Paperclip (1,500 private documents, all 15 answers must be right) and AA-Symmetry (does the answer change when the question is reworded). Among decision models, Nace AI's Drex Max v1.1 and Fastino's GLiDE v1.2 both score 73, and Base Labs' Mammoth 27B scores 72. Claude Haiku 5.5 (max) 77 and GPT-6 Luna (max) 76 cost more and run slower: AA lists Drex Max at $102 per million tasks and 275 ms per task, against $1,530 and 11.34 seconds for Luna. Not a Ridge board. Source: https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/decision-index-v2

News (2026-11-06): OpenAI BioBasicsBench, 100 routine wet-lab analysis tasks built with Ligo. Agents interpret supplied evidence, not a physical lab. OpenAI's own xhigh measurements: GPT-6 Astra 66.7% of available rubric credit, GPT-5.6 Sol 43.8%, five attempts per task. Mean reward is partial credit, not experiment completion or a straight accuracy score. The article shows Astra misreading controls, dismissing contradictory evidence and miscounting colonies. Task review is not an independent replication. No dataset download or license in the write-up. Not a Ridge board. Source: https://openai.com/index/measuring-how-ai-agents-handle-wet-lab-science

News (2026-10-05): Reflection AI announced Beam, a 501B-parameter (23B active) open-weight model; weights due later in October under Apache 2.0. Not on the board yet: no independent scores. Benchmark claims are Reflection's own. Source: https://reflection.ai/blog/introducing-beam
New column (2026-10-04): AA Cyber Index. Grok 4.7 56 (xhigh), GPT-6 Luna 53 (max), Muse Spark 1.3 44 (xhigh), Kimi K3 41, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 41, GPT-6 Sol 37, GLM-5.3 36, GPT-6 Astra 33, Claude Opus 5.5 29, Gemini 3.8 Flash 25, Claude Fable 5.1 25. GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Gemini 3.8 Flash decline about a third of tasks on safety grounds. Other catalog models are blank.
New model (2026-09-30): Gemini 4 Argon (Google DeepMind, limited preview for Fairwind cyber defenders), intro $2 / $10 then $4 / $20 per 1M tokens, 1M output limit. AA 53, Arena+ 1525; no CursorBench, Terminal-Bench, or SWE-bench yet.
New model (2026-09-29): GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI, DevDay), $2 / $10 per 1M tokens, 1M context. AA 52, Arena+ 1516; no CursorBench, Terminal-Bench, or SWE-bench yet.
New model (2026-09-28): Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Anthropic, claude-sonnet-5-5), $2 / $10 per 1M tokens, 1M context. AA 56, CursorBench 4.0 55.5, Arena+ 1521, Vals Terminal-Bench 2.1 83.15; no SWE-bench yet.
News (2026-09-24): UN Security Council AI session (Altman and Amodei call for global standards; Trump rejects global AI regulation). China's CAC probes DeepSeek and Moonshot over alleged Claude distillation (Decrypt / The Information; follows Anthropic's 10 Sep threat report). First public-opinion ratings: Opus 5.5 4, GPT-6 Sol 3, GPT-6 Luna 3, Grok 4.7 3; earlier ratings unchanged. No board score changes. 23 Sep: METR Opus 5.5 eval; price-war desk note; ChatGPT Voice on Astra/Sol/Luna; SWE-Together audit; Vals Terminal-Bench Sol 83.15 / Luna 73.03. 22 Sep: Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol/Luna launches with first-party board scores.
